meta.purpose: Negative-polarity teaching-evaluation items. Kept separate from questions.json so a generator drop does not overwrite them.
meta.form: Which statement indicates a need for further teaching? Three options are correct teaching and are eliminated. The keyed answer is the one statement that is wrong.
meta.note: Trimmed once the generator began producing its own further-teaching items. Only ids the bank does not already use are kept.

items.stem: A nurse reviews medications with an older adult who takes eight prescriptions. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should bring every bottle, including vitamins and herbal products, to my visits
options.rationale: Correct. Over-the-counter and herbal products count toward polypharmacy and interact.

options.text: Anything I can buy without a prescription is safe to add on my own
options.rationale: This is the error. Over-the-counter products interact with prescriptions, and several are on lists of medications to avoid in older adults.

options.text: If a pill makes me feel dizzy I should tell the clinic rather than stop it myself
options.rationale: Correct. Reporting allows the regimen to be adjusted safely.

options.text: Using one pharmacy helps them catch interactions between my medicines
options.rationale: Correct. A single pharmacy record improves interaction screening.

items.takeaway: Over-the-counter does not mean risk-free, and it counts toward the medication total.
items.strategy: The key treats a category of drug as automatically safe. Absolutes about safety are rarely correct.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It declares an entire category safe.

elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A preceptor teaches a new graduate how to set priorities. Which statement by the graduate indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: Airway and breathing problems come before circulation problems
options.rationale: Correct. The ABC sequence orders life threats.

options.text: An actual problem generally comes before a risk of a problem
options.rationale: Correct. Actual problems usually outrank potential ones.

options.text: A change in mental status can be an early sign of deterioration
options.rationale: Correct. Acute mental status change is often the first sign that something is wrong.

options.text: Whatever the client asks for first should be done first
options.rationale: This is the error. Requests matter, but urgency is set by clinical risk, not by order of asking.

items.takeaway: Priority follows threat to life, not the order requests arrive in.
items.strategy: Three options use a clinical framework. The key uses sequence of asking.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: Only one option orders care by request rather than risk.

elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches a student how to conduct an admission interview. Which statement by the student indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should start with open-ended questions and narrow down from there
options.rationale: Correct. Open questions gather the client's own account before focusing.

options.text: I should ask the most sensitive questions first to get them out of the way
options.rationale: This is the error. Sensitive topics come after rapport is established. Leading with them reduces disclosure.

options.text: I should summarize at the end so the client can correct me
options.rationale: Correct. Validation improves accuracy.

options.text: I should ask one question at a time rather than stacking several together
options.rationale: Correct. Stacked questions produce incomplete answers.

items.takeaway: Rapport first, sensitive questions later. Sequence affects what the client is willing to tell you.
items.strategy: Three options improve accuracy. The key trades rapport for speed.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false
elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches a student about collaborative problems. Which statement by the student indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: A collaborative problem needs both nursing and provider interventions
options.rationale: Correct. Collaborative problems require both.

options.text: Monitoring for postoperative hemorrhage is a collaborative problem
options.rationale: Correct. The nurse monitors and reports, and treatment requires a provider.

options.text: Nursing diagnoses are treated primarily by independent nursing actions
options.rationale: Correct. That independence is what distinguishes them.

options.text: Because a collaborative problem needs a provider, nursing has no independent role
options.rationale: This is the error. Surveillance, early detection, and reporting are independent nursing responsibilities and are often what determines the outcome.

items.takeaway: Collaborative does not mean passive. Monitoring and escalation are independent nursing actions.
items.strategy: The key draws a false conclusion from a true premise.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It moves from needs a provider to nursing has no role.

elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches a student to prioritize a care plan using Maslow. Which statement by the student indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: Physiological needs generally come before self-esteem needs
options.rationale: Correct. Lower-level needs are addressed first.

options.text: Psychosocial needs can wait until every physical need is fully resolved
options.rationale: This is the error. The hierarchy guides priority, not sequence. Psychosocial needs are addressed alongside physical ones, and in some situations they take precedence.

options.text: Safety needs come before love and belonging needs
options.rationale: Correct ordering within the hierarchy.

options.text: A client's stated priority should be considered alongside the framework
options.rationale: Correct. The client's own priority is part of planning.

items.takeaway: Maslow orders priority, not permission. Psychosocial care runs in parallel with physical care.
items.strategy: The key turns a guide into a rigid rule. Watch for every and fully.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It requires every physical need resolved first.

elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: An instructor teaches students about nursing interventions. Which statement by a student indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: Repositioning a client to prevent pressure injury is an independent intervention
options.rationale: Correct. It requires no order.

options.text: Administering a prescribed medication is a dependent intervention
options.rationale: Correct. It follows a provider order.

options.text: Working with the dietitian on a feeding plan is a collaborative intervention
options.rationale: Correct. It involves another discipline.

options.text: If an order seems wrong I should carry it out and document my concern afterward
options.rationale: This is the error. The nurse must clarify a questionable order before acting. Carrying it out and documenting afterward does not transfer liability.

items.takeaway: Question the order before you carry it out. Documenting a concern does not make an unsafe action safe.
items.strategy: The key sounds procedurally careful while still performing the unsafe act.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It acts first and questions second.

elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A preceptor teaches a new graduate about revising a plan of care. Which statement by the graduate indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: If the client's condition changes, the plan should change with it
options.rationale: Correct. The plan is dynamic.

options.text: A plan written on admission should stay unchanged so the record is consistent
options.rationale: This is the error. A static plan stops reflecting the client. Consistency of the record is maintained by documenting changes, not by avoiding them.

options.text: I should discontinue an intervention that is no longer needed
options.rationale: Correct. Resolved problems are closed out.

options.text: The client should be involved when goals are revised
options.rationale: Correct. Revision is mutual, like the original planning.

items.takeaway: A care plan that never changes is a care plan nobody is using.
items.strategy: The key protects the document at the expense of the client.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false
elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A preceptor teaches a new graduate how to escalate a concern about a deteriorating client. Which statement by the graduate indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should use a structured format such as SBAR so the message is clear
options.rationale: Correct. Structure reduces omissions under pressure.

options.text: I should state clearly what I am asking the provider to do
options.rationale: Correct. The recommendation is the part most often left out.

options.text: I should document what I reported, when, and the response
options.rationale: Correct. The record of escalation matters clinically and legally.

options.text: If the provider does not respond I should keep waiting rather than go over their head
options.rationale: This is the error. When a client is deteriorating and a concern is unanswered, the nurse is obligated to escalate through the chain of command.

items.takeaway: Escalation is a duty, not a discourtesy. An unanswered concern about a deteriorating client goes up the chain.
items.strategy: The key frames advocacy as rudeness. Client safety outranks hierarchy.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false
elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches a client about advance directives. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I can change or cancel my advance directive at any time
options.rationale: Correct. It is revocable while the client has capacity.

options.text: Once I sign this, I cannot change my mind later
options.rationale: This is the error. Advance directives are not binding on the person who made them and may be revised or revoked at any time.

options.text: My health care proxy speaks for me only if I cannot speak for myself
options.rationale: Correct. The proxy acts on incapacity.

options.text: Having a directive does not mean I will receive less care
options.rationale: Correct. A directive guides which treatments are wanted, not the quality of care.

items.takeaway: An advance directive is revocable as long as the client has capacity. It records wishes, it does not lock them.
items.strategy: Look for the option that removes a right the client retains.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It says the decision cannot be changed.

elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse manager teaches staff about incident reports. Which statement by a nurse indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I complete an incident report even if the client was not injured
options.rationale: Correct. Events are reported regardless of outcome.

options.text: I should document the clinical facts of the event in the client's record
options.rationale: Correct. The clinical event and the client's condition belong in the record.

options.text: Filing a report is not an admission that anyone did something wrong
options.rationale: Correct. Reports document events, not fault.

options.text: I should write in the chart that an incident report was completed
options.rationale: This is the error. The incident report is a quality-improvement document and is not referenced in the medical record.

items.takeaway: Chart the event, not the paperwork. Referencing an incident report in the record pulls it into the legal chart.
items.strategy: Three options separate the record from the report. The key links them.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It names the report in the chart.

elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches a student to communicate with a client who is hard of hearing. Which statement by the student indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should face the client so they can see my mouth
options.rationale: Correct. Visual cues support comprehension.

options.text: I should raise my voice and speak in a higher pitch so it carries
options.rationale: This is the error. Age-related hearing loss affects high frequencies first, so raising pitch makes speech harder to understand. Speak lower and more clearly rather than louder.

options.text: I should reduce background noise before we talk
options.rationale: Correct. Competing noise is a major barrier.

options.text: I should confirm understanding rather than assume a nod means yes
options.rationale: Correct. Nodding often signals social politeness rather than comprehension.

items.takeaway: Lower and clearer, not louder and higher. High frequencies are the first to go.
items.strategy: The key follows intuition. Ask which frequencies are actually lost.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It raises the frequency the client hears worst.

elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches staff about health literacy. Which statement by a nurse indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should use plain language rather than clinical terms
options.rationale: Correct. Plain language improves comprehension for everyone.

options.text: Limited health literacy is not the same as low intelligence
options.rationale: Correct. They are unrelated.

options.text: Written material should supplement rather than replace conversation
options.rationale: Correct. Handouts reinforce teaching but do not substitute for it.

options.text: Asking do you understand is enough to confirm learning
options.rationale: This is the error. Clients commonly answer yes regardless of comprehension. Teach-back, asking them to explain it in their own words, is the standard.

items.takeaway: Do you understand invites a yes. Ask the client to explain it back instead.
items.strategy: The key is the most common shortcut in real practice, which is exactly why it is tested.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It relies on the client self-reporting understanding.

elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches staff about privacy in the electronic health record. Which statement by a nurse indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should log out rather than leave a workstation open
options.rationale: Correct. An open session allows access under the nurse's credentials.

options.text: I may look up a family member's record if I am only checking they are all right
options.rationale: This is the error. Access is limited to clients in the nurse's care. Curiosity and concern are not treatment relationships, and access is audited.

options.text: I should not discuss clients in elevators or corridors
options.rationale: Correct. Overheard conversation is a common breach.

options.text: I should not share my login even with a colleague who has forgotten theirs
options.rationale: Correct. Credentials are individual and every action is attributed to them.

items.takeaway: Access requires a treatment relationship. Good intentions are not authorization, and the audit log does not record intent.
items.strategy: The key supplies a sympathetic motive. Motive does not create access rights.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It opens a record without a care relationship.

elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: An instructor teaches students about crisis intervention. Which statement by a student indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: A crisis happens when usual coping methods stop working
options.rationale: Correct definition of crisis.

options.text: Crisis intervention focuses on the immediate problem rather than long-standing issues
options.rationale: Correct. It is short term and present focused.

options.text: Safety is assessed first when someone is in crisis
options.rationale: Correct. Safety precedes everything else.

options.text: If a client says there is no reason to keep going, I should note it and raise it at the next team meeting
options.rationale: This is the error. A statement of hopelessness requires immediate direct assessment of suicidal ideation, not deferral.

items.takeaway: Any statement suggesting the client sees no future is assessed now, directly, not deferred.
items.strategy: Three options are definitions. The key is an action, and it delays.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false
elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse teaches a client newly prescribed continuous positive airway pressure for obstructive sleep apnea. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I should wear it every night, including naps
options.rationale: Correct. Apnea occurs whenever the client sleeps.

options.text: Once I feel more rested I can stop using it
options.rationale: This is the error. Feeling better is the treatment working, not the condition resolving. Apnea returns as soon as the device is stopped.

options.text: If the mask leaks or hurts I should ask about a refitting rather than stop using it
options.rationale: Correct. Fit problems are solvable and are a leading cause of abandonment.

options.text: Losing weight may reduce the severity, but I should keep using it until I am reassessed
options.rationale: Correct. Weight loss can help, but therapy continues until reassessment.

items.takeaway: Improvement on therapy is not cure. This is the same error as stopping an antihypertensive because the pressure is now normal.
items.strategy: The key uses symptom relief as evidence the problem is gone.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It discontinues therapy on feeling better.

elimination.verdict: B is the statement needing correction.

items.stem: A nurse reviews self-care with a client who has type 2 diabetes. Which statement by the client indicates a need for further teaching?

options.text: I will inspect my feet daily, including between the toes
options.rationale: Correct. Daily inspection detects injury early when sensation is reduced.

options.text: I will report any sore that is not healing rather than wait for my next visit
options.rationale: Correct. Non-healing wounds need prompt assessment.

options.text: I will keep glucose tablets with me in case my sugar drops
options.rationale: Correct. Fast-acting carbohydrate should be carried.

options.text: I will soak my feet in hot water each evening to keep them soft
options.rationale: This is the error. Soaking macerates skin, and reduced sensation from neuropathy means the client may not feel water that is hot enough to burn.

items.takeaway: No soaking and no hot water. Neuropathy means the client cannot rely on sensation to judge temperature or injury.
items.strategy: The key sounds like self-care. Ask what reduced sensation makes unsafe.

strategies: Treat each option as true or false

steps.detail: It relies on sensation the client may not have.

elimination.verdict: D is the statement needing correction.
